notes: §1985:X.5.2.4 GR3 requires that a CALL whose program 'cannot be made available for execution' transfer to imperative-statement-1 when ON OVERFLOW or ON EXCEPTION is written (then to the end of the CALL, NOT ON EXCEPTION ignored), and otherwise leaves 'All other effects' to the implementor. ProgramTable#Activate (via CallProgram) throws CobolCallException for a name ResolveVisible cannot locate, a stack it cannot get, or an active non-recursive program; CallBinder#BindCall binds the 85 ON OVERFLOW as the same ON branch (onExc ??= onOverflow), and CallEmitter#EmitCall catches the failure into imperative-statement-1 and guards NOT ON EXCEPTION with the failure flag (EmitNotOnException); with no ON phrase the run unit ends abnormally with a message, the documented implementor choice, and NOT ON never runs. Probes at --std 85: ON OVERFLOW miss printed OVF; identifier-1 with GO TO in imperative-1 transferred; ref-modified identifier-1 at its bound (1:8) took ON EXCEPTION; found program ran NOT ON; a self-CALL of an active program took ON EXCEPTION; NOT ON only without ON on a miss printed nothing and ended abnormally (rc 1); refusals: ON OVERFLOW plus NOT ON EXCEPTION (COBOL2269), RETURNING (COBOL0884, 2002+), numeric identifier-1 (COBOL1681), empty imperative (COBOL2072), ON EXCEPTION twice (COBOL2269). The witness exercises a literal miss with both phrases.
